title: Metabolic health in neurodegenerative diseases - implications of metabolic characteristics and gut microbiome
summary:
Among neurodegenerative diseases, Alzheimer's disease (AD) and primary Parkinson's syndrome (PD), represent the leading causes of mortality and loss of quality of life in the elderly worldwide. Despite extensive research, the underlying reason for the aforementioned diseases is still unclear. At the same time the number of people with metabolic diseases, such as diabetes or high blood pressure, is rapidly increasing.  Interestingly, people with diabetes were at higher risk to develop AD or PD. One factor that has a role in both, the neurodegenerative and metabolic diseases mentioned, is the composition of the intestinal microbiome, i.e. the colonization of the intestines with microorganisms. The gut microbiome is significantly influenced by nutritional aspects and is crucial for maintaining healthy conditions or promoting diseases.
The aim of this explorative human study is to research markers of metabolic health in individuals with AD and PD in association with the gut microbiome and thereof derived metabolic products and to compare them with individuals who have metabolic syndrome. Among others, the composition and function of the microbiome (using high-throughput methods), markers of sugar and fat metabolism, inflammatory markers of the body and brain as well as genetic parameters will be assessed. In addition, the nutritional behavior will be examined.

interventions.name:
People with Parkinson disease

Participation in the study consists of two visits. On visit 1, inclusion in the study takes place after the inclusion and exclusion criteria have been checked. In addition,  a detailed explanation of the study measurements is done and study questionnaires are handed

People with Alzheimer disease

The study procedure is identical to that described for Arm 1.

People with metabolic syndrome

The study procedure is identical to that described for Arm 1.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
•	BMI 18,5-39,9 kg/m²
•	Non-smoker (for at least 3 months)
written declaration of consent for participation in the study.
•	Diagnosis Parkinson disease or Alzheimer disease 

PD cohort:
•	PD based on clinical diagnosis according to Brain Bank criteria(Hughes AJ, Daniel SE, Kilford L, Lees AJ. Accuracy of clinical diagnosis of idiopathic Parkinson’s disease. A clinico-pathological study of 100 cases. JNNP 1992;55:181-184.)
•	Hoehn & Yahr stadium 1-3

AD cohort
•	Clinical and biomarker-based diagnosis with Alzheimer's pathology based on typical CSF findings
Mixed dementia with a vascular component (up to Fazekas II) is permitted.
Exclusion criteria:
•	Taking medications that affect glucose metabolism
•	chronic inflammatory bowel or liver diseases
•	antibiotic therapy 3 weeks before the start of the study
•	Planned lifestyle changes
•	regular intake of supplements
•	drug abuse
•	participation in another clinical trial simultaneously/in the last 30 days

PD cohort:
•	Atypical PD syndromes
•	DBS care
•	severe motor fluctuations

AD cohort:
•	Dementia of unclear origin
•	Heavy vascular part (Fazekas III)
